name: ARPL index
description: Machine-readable index of ARPL instruction packs. Generated by tools/build_catalogs.py; read AGENTS.md for how to use it.
staleness: Two triggers. review_due is one year after the last evidence (recorded date or latest reproduction). unverified_in_current_revit is true when the pack was not tested in the latest Revit release (vocabularies revit_releases). Either one: verify the result as if the pack were new.
provenance: Record every pack you used as {arpl_pack, pack_revision, revit_version, result}. To pin exact content, replace main in raw_base with a commit SHA or release tag.

work_classes.W1: Component family authoring (driven by a source and an LOD)
work_classes.W2: Adaptive / form-driven geometry (driven by a rig)
work_classes.W3: Layout-driven assembly production (driven by a rule applied many times)
work_classes.W4: Building model authoring (driven by a program and system families)
work_classes.W5: Model change and propagation (driven by one changed fundamental)
work_classes.W6: Documentation production (driven by views and sheets)
work_classes.W7: Information and data (driven by parameters, standards, quantities)
work_classes.W8: Analysis and review (driven by questions about an existing model)

project_workflows.title: ADU exterior wall fabrication package (LOD 400 + BOM)
project_workflows.intent: Turn the exterior walls of a one-storey wood-frame ADU into prefabricated wall panels: 2x6 framing, 3/4in plywood, bevel siding, XPS cavity fill; one assembly per wall; shop drawings; BOM and cost.

steps.do: Build and flex-test component families (lumber, sheet panel, insulation block, siding board)
Write the layout rule (studs 16in o.c., 3-stud corners, double top plate lapped, openings with king/jack/header/sill/cripples, sheets on stud centres, siding courses, foam per cavity)
2D preview from the rule: studs in plan, sheet and board joints in elevations; user confirms or corrects the rule
Resolve design conflicts found by the preview as user decisions (door lowered to fit a header) and re-preview
Replay the rule in 3D per wall; disallow joins on all framing; verify every piece; group into assemblies
Assembly shop drawings: framing and sheathing elevations, plan section, 3D, part list; trade dimension style; PDF review
Quantities and cost from the model; governed BOM parameters
Issue: one shop drawing sheet per panel that differs (identical panels once, with a quantity), add every assembly sheet to the print set, export the set to PDF, open the PDF and check each sheet
Synchronize with central after the package passes its checks, with a comment; on cloud models save local before and after (operating rule in AGENTS.md)

project_workflows.title: ADU shed roof assembly (LOD 400 + BOM): framing, deck, standing seam, trim, insulation
project_workflows.intent: Replace a placeholder shed roof with a real build-up and turn it into one roof assembly: 2x8 rafters @ 24in, walls rebuilt to fit the roof (taller high wall, raked end walls), frieze blocks, outlookers and fly rafters, 3/4in plywood deck, standing seam roofing, 1x10 fascia and barge boards covering every exposed rafter cut, batts and drywall inside the wall lines, shop drawing and BOM with cost.

steps.do: Read the roof as modelled before planning: type, slope, footprint, overhangs, height gap between flat wall plates and the sloped roof underside, neighbouring elements (e.g. a trellis under the eave)

Ask the decisions that belong to the user: structure (rafters on walls built to fit the roof vs trusses), member size (engineer flag), roofing for the slope (5 deg excludes asphalt shingles), overhangs, trim, soffit, insulation, assembly grouping
2D preview from the layout rule: framing plan, sheathing plan, section; check every view direction; look at the exported images

Replace the placeholder roof: new footprint roof with the real layers (Revit 2024 cannot edit roof sketches or attach walls by API), user re-attaches the walls, then delete the old roof; guard every transaction
Component families: lumber types 2x8 / 2x4 flat; work-plane-based copies of sheet and insulation families; flex-test the plane orientation

Build from one layout rule in a dry run with an all-pairs clash check; offset square-cut ends by depth x sin(slope); commit only with allow-listed contacts; trim must cover every exposed cut; insulation only inside the exterior wall lines
Create the assembly after Regenerate; name it after commit
BOM from the model: check every piece against its stock size; reset Cost and Type Comments on duplicated types; price with source and date; stock conversion, waste, tax, range
Shop drawing: framing plan with deck hidden, deck layout, section along the slope, 3D, parts list, dimensions one per transaction, BOM note; export and look at the sheet

packs.title: Assembly naming and identical panels

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: creating and naming Revit assemblies
several identical panels or modules need drawings
packs.rule: Name assemblies after commit; document identical assemblies once with a quantity ('build 2'). Identical panels may share one assembly type only while their geometry stays identical. When they diverge (raked end walls are mirror images, not copies), give each its own type before editing members: changing the members of one instance of a shared type opens a modal Revit dialog no script can answer and copies the change to the other instances (FP15). An assembly made with AssemblyInstance.Create gets a frame along the project axes; set it with SetTransform (BasisX along the wall, BasisY to the interior) before creating its views (FP16).
validation: Assembly type names and member counts read back

packs.title: Device placement follows the framing (manufacturer's standpoint)

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 with run_csharp

use_when: placing receptacles, switches, lights, smoke alarms, floor boxes or other devices in framed walls, roofs or floors
layout previews for prefab wall, roof or floor panels
not_for: devices on concrete or masonry without framing (use slab sleeve / chase rules)
deciding code compliance (the code checks still apply)
packs.rule: Place every device the way the panel manufacturer would build it: the framing is part of the layout from the first preview, not a correction at rough-in. 1) Build the layout preview on top of the framing layout (studs, plates, headers, rafters or joists, blocking, sheathing joints), not on the room outline alone. 2) Walls: box beside a stud, never on it (single-gang centre 47 mm from the stud axis, 2-gang and round boxes 75 mm), on the side that keeps the cavity widest; keep clear of corner and king/jack studs, headers, plates and sheathing joints; one standard height per device type (receptacles 300 mm, counter 1,100 mm, switches 1,220 mm) unless the code or the owner says otherwise. 3) Roofs and ceilings: devices centred in the rafter or joist bay where the room allows; minimum clearance 19 mm + device radius + 10 mm from the member axis; driver and junction boxes inside the same bay. 4) Floors: floor boxes, registers and drains in the joist bay (or in planned slab sleeves), never through a joist or beam. 5) Prefer devices on prefab panels in bays that are open in the factory; group devices so one bay or one wire run serves several. 6) After moving a device for the framing, re-run the code checks (NEC spacing) before modelling.
validation: Every wall box ≥ required distance from every stud axis (report the minimum)
Every ceiling device ≥ clearance from every rafter or joist axis and inside its room
NEC spacing checks still pass after framing moves
Rough-in clash check: only soft layers cut

packs.title: Vertical studs pulled by auto-joins

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: placing vertical studs, posts or braces as structural framing
framing members end up longer or shifted after placement
not_for: structural columns (not framing)
packs.rule: Disallow joins on all framing members immediately at creation and verify positions after regeneration.
validation: Interference check between all assemblies
Stud end heights read back

packs.title: Door too tall for a header

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: framing a wall with openings where headers must fit under top plates
a door or window rough opening is close to the plate height
not_for: openings in non-framed walls (masonry, concrete)
packs.rule: Report every opening whose rough opening plus header doesn't fit under the plates as a decision for the user; never move a header into the top plates. Size each header from the span tables for its opening and the load it carries (bearing wall under rafters vs non-bearing); never default to the stud size. Splitting a long opening into standard units with posts turns an engineered beam into table-sized headers.
validation: Rough opening and header heights dimensioned on the shop drawing
Header size per opening reported with its span and bearing condition

packs.title: Plywood slivers at openings

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: laying out sheathing, sheet goods or cladding boards across a wall with openings
deciding where panel joints fall relative to windows and doors
not_for: curtain walls
single full-height sheets without openings
packs.rule: Minimum remnant width is a parameter of the layout rule and is evaluated on both sides of every opening edge.
validation: Measured joint positions in the preview
Piece-by-piece check of the 3D build

packs.title: Slab on grade from the framing layout (anchors, recess, stub-ups)

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 with run_csharp

use_when: a prefab timber building sits on a slab on grade
anchor bolts, slab recesses or plumbing stub-ups must match wall panels and fixtures
not_for: structural design of the slab or anchorage (engineer of record)
raised floors on piers or ground screws
packs.rule: 1) Take the slab edge from the framing outer faces and the anchor lines from the bottom-plate segments of the current wall panels; at door openings there is no plate and no anchor. 2) Place anchors per plate segment: max spacing and end distance from the engineer (assumed 1219 / 305 mm), at least two per segment, clear of stud axes. 3) Keep stub-ups out of the thickened edge and record them from one slab corner. 4) A curbless shower is a slab recess with the full slab thickness below it; subtract it from the edge beam where they meet. 5) Show the 2D layout and BOM for review, then model it as one assembly (slab floor, recess floor, edge as Structural Foundation DirectShape, bolts, stub-ups) and clash-check it against the wall assemblies: bolts through bottom plates are intended. 6) Re-derive the anchors whenever a wall panel is rebuilt.
validation: Anchor report per plate segment: count, max gap, end distances, min distance to a stud axis
Stub-ups outside the thickened edge (except where intended)
Clash check against wall assemblies: only bolt x bottom plate / insulation
Placeholder host dependents checked before deletion

packs.title: Sloped roof assembly from component families

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: framing and finishing a sloped (shed, mono-pitch) roof as an assembly of lumber, sheet and board families
placing sheet goods, insulation or trim on a sloped plane
covering rafter tails and fly rafters with fascia and barge boards
not_for: prefabricated trusses modelled as single families
curved roofs
packs.rule: 1) Check family placement type before reuse; make work-plane-based copies under new names. 2) Flex-test the plane orientation (cut vector sign) with one instance and read back the transform. 3) Compute every sloped member from one layout rule; offset square-cut ends by depth x sin(slope); members that carry the deck (outlookers, flat blocking) are rotated to the slope (cross-section rotation = slope angle; check the sign by the top-face normal), with their top on the rafter-top plane. 4) Dry-run the whole build with an all-pairs clash check and commit only when every remaining contact is on an allow-list of intended conditions. 5) Verify that trim covers every exposed cut by comparing end-face extents with trim extents. 6) Before documenting, check every modelled piece against its stock size (no piece longer than the sheet or board it is cut from). 7) After Duplicate(), reset Cost, Type Comments and other data parameters of every new type; duplicated types inherit them silently. 8) Insulation (batts, foam) runs only inside the exterior wall lines, bearing to bearing; eaves and rake overhangs are not insulated. 9) Walls are built to fit the roof, as a prefab plant would: no wedge or pony wall. The high wall is framed taller (cap at the rafter bearing), the end walls are raked (sloped double top plate, studs cut to it), and sheathing, insulation and siding are cut to the rafter line inside the wall panels. The roof assembly holds only roof components. The design (host) walls follow the roof too: sloped wall profile on the raked walls, raised top on the high wall; the wall gypsum stops under the ceiling drywall (rafter line minus the drywall thickness), so the ceiling board runs over the wall top. 10) Before changing the members of an assembly instance, check whether its type is shared by other instances; if so, build a new assembly (AssemblyInstance.Create) instead, because Revit asks a modal question no script can answer and then copies the change to every instance (FP15). Box families cannot make sloped edges: use DirectShape extrusions with material and Comments/Mark for the BOM.
validation: Flex test transform equals expected axes
Clash check: only allow-listed contacts
End faces of all rafters, fly rafters and outlookers inside fascia/barge extents
Assembly member count equals pieces built
No piece longer than its stock length
Every type in the assembly has its own Cost and unit in Type Comments
Insulation bounding box inside the outer face of the wall framing (ADU-01: batts y -1134.1..2456.2 within -1172.7..2494.8; x -3944.9..8002.7 within -3983..8040.8)
Top-face normal of every deck-bearing member equals the roof normal
Every exterior face below the roof is closed: framing, insulation, sheathing, siding and gypsum reach the rafter line on all walls

test_runs.note: after parameterization: kind falls back to Category: Family Type

inputs.ASSEMBLY_PREFIXES: assembly type name prefixes, empty = all assemblies
inputs.ALLOW: intended contacts, 'Kind A x Kind B'

model_assumptions: The pieces to check are members of assemblies
Piece kind comes from Comments when filled (ARPL build scripts), otherwise from Category: Family Type
Solid geometry exists for every piece (DirectShapes and family instances); linked models are not checked
not_for: Clash checks between linked models (use Navisworks or a link-aware check)
Proving structural adequacy: a clash-free model can still be wrong

packs.title: Residential branch circuits from a confirmed layout

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 with run_csharp

use_when: electrical for a small dwelling unit or ADU: panel, receptacles, lighting, smoke alarms, circuits
placing wall and ceiling devices by API on host-wall faces and ceiling planes
creating circuits and a panel schedule by API
not_for: commercial distribution or three-phase systems
load calculations or code compliance sign-off (electrical engineer / AHJ)
conduit or cable routing
packs.rule: 1) Lay out devices in 2D first, on top of the framing layout (ARPL-ASM-0007), and check them against NEC 210.52 (wall spacing 1.83 m, counter 600 mm, bath basin 900 mm, front/back exterior, HVAC service receptacle 7.5 m) before modelling; the owner confirms. 2) Check what content exists; author missing families from Family Templates with PowerBalanced connectors (ARPL-CON-0001); wall-mounted ones from 'Electrical Fixture.rft' (switch category if needed), not from 'Lighting Fixture.rft'. 3) Place wall devices on host-wall side faces, fetching fresh face references for every placement (FP18); ceiling devices on a horizontal reference plane at the finished ceiling. 4) Before circuiting, probe the panel's supply connector (voltage, poles) against the distribution system; template commercial panelboards are 208 V 3-pole. Probe device loads (some types carry 0 VA). 5) Create circuits in the order of the planned numbering; for loads above 80 % of the default 20 A rating expect a modal warning during ElectricalSystem.Create (FP17): watch the screen, or create them with a temporary small load. 6) Place the panel schedule, export the sheet as an image and look at it; sync after the checks pass. 7) Before rough-in, check every device against the framing: wall box centre ≥ 19 + half box width + 3 mm from a stud axis (47 mm single-gang, 75 mm round 4 in), ceiling device ≥ 19 + radius + 10 mm from a rafter axis and inside its room; move the device, then re-run the NEC spacing check. 8) Model the rough-in as members of the prefab assemblies (boxes, cut-outs, sleeves, nipples) and clash-check them: only insulation, sheathing, siding and drywall may be cut, never framing. Partition walls built on site get no rough-in pieces. 9) Re-run the wall-space check whenever doors or windows change: fixed panels of sliding glass doors count as wall space and the operable panels are doorways, so posts between standard sliders usually need their own receptacle. A wall panel rebuild deletes the rough-in in that assembly; re-run it for that wall only.
validation: NEC 210.52 spacing checks pass on the 2D layout
Every device placed within 2 mm of its face (report distance)
Panel connector voltage/poles match the distribution system
Circuit numbers equal the planned numbers; ratings and loads read back
Panel schedule and sheet exported and inspected
Rough-in clash check: only soft layers cut (XPS, plywood, siding, drywall, batt)
Wall-space check re-run after every opening change

packs.title: Shop drawings: invalid references and swapped elevations

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: creating dimensioned shop drawings or assembly sheets
adding many dimensions by script
packs.rule: Isolate risky annotation in its own transaction and verify every sheet visually. Regenerate the shop drawing whenever the assembly members are replaced: dimensions reference member faces and are deleted with them. DirectShape faces take dimension references like family geometry. Sloped faces cannot be dimensioned in an elevation chain; state the heights at both ends in a note on the view. Check the assembly frame first (FP16). When rescaling: crop plans to the building first (clear scope boxes, which override the crop), turn on annotation crop, trim section width and far clip, hide markers that a template will not let you hide by category (HideElements), then re-pack sheets and check every viewport against the drawing area. A single-view sheet is centred, never emptied; continuation sheets (<number>A) only for real overflow on multi-view sheets (FP23).
validation: PDF export rendered and reviewed per sheet
Every viewport inside the title block drawing area and no overlaps after a scale change

packs.title: Gable walls without wall attachment

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.3.0 with run_csharp

use_when: walls under gable or sloped roofs
walls that should follow a roof slope
packs.rule: Use profile walls for gables and register them as dependents of the roof and the levels. Revit 2024 API: an existing wall's profile can be edited: Wall.CreateProfileSketch() in its own transaction, then SketchEditScope.Start(sketch.Id), replace the curves with NewModelCurve on sketch.SketchPlane, and commit the scope with a failures preprocessor. (Footprint roof sketches cannot be edited this way.) Walls under a sloped roof take a profile that follows the rafter line, minus the ceiling drywall so the ceiling board runs over the wall top.
validation: Section view check

packs.title: Footing corner notches

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: modelling foundations or footings at wall corners

packs.rule: Model corner conditions explicitly; never rely on automatic joins.
validation: Plan and 3D check of footing corners

packs.title: An exception inside an open Transaction crashed Revit

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp

use_when: any scripted change that starts its own Transaction, especially inside a TransactionGroup
a bridge or add-in runs agent-written C# against a live model
not_for: read-only scripts that open no transaction
packs.rule: Wrap every own Transaction (and SubTransaction) in using(...) so it is rolled back during exception unwinding, before any enclosing group is aborted. Wrap the script body in try/catch and return the failing step. Dry-run every new API call first. Bridges should run 'group' mode snippets so that unwinding happens before the group is rolled back.
validation: Dry run of the guarded script returns the error and step instead of crashing
Journal shows no 'Undo phases not properly nested' warnings

packs.title: Reset a workshared cloud model: remove all Revit links and delete user worksets with all worksets closed

environment.tool: RevitBridge 0.4.0 (local Revit API bridge, MCP) with run_csharp
environment.model: 10 workshared ACC cloud test models (generic test project)

use_when: batch-clean several workshared cloud (ACC/BIM 360) models before a relinking run, a demo or a standards reset
delete user worksets and move their elements to Workset1 without opening the worksets
remove every RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance from a host model
not_for: detaching or archiving models (use DetachFromCentral instead)
non-workshared files
removing CAD imports or links (ImportInstance, CADLinkType)
packs.rule: Per model, in one bridge call of at most 2-3 models (each cloud open+sync takes 15-25 s): 1) open by cloud GUIDs (ConvertCloudGUIDsToCloudPath) with WorksetConfiguration(CloseAllWorksets) and DoNotDetach; closed worksets are enough for both tasks and keep the open fast. 2) Delete all RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance ids in one Transaction with a failures preprocessor. 3) Collect user worksets; keep Workset1 and the shared levels/grids workset. Call WorksharingUtils.CheckoutWorksets on the worksets to delete plus Workset1 (works while they are closed); make Workset1 active. 4) In a Transaction, for each workset: DeleteWorksetSettings(MoveElementsToWorkset, Workset1), CanDeleteWorkset, then DeleteWorkset; collect failures per workset instead of aborting. 5) SynchronizeWithCentral with SaveLocalBefore and SaveLocalAfter true, RelinquishOptions(true) and a comment; skip the sync when nothing changed. 6) Close(false) in finally. Return per-model counts and timings. Check free disk space first: every cloud open fills the local collaboration cache.
validation: Re-open check: RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance counts are 0
User worksets are exactly Workset1 plus the shared levels/grids workset
No elements or worksets remain borrowed after sync (relinquished)
Sync comment visible in the cloud model's version history

failure_patterns.name: Geometry correct, semantics wrong
failure_patterns.meaning: The shape is right but the category, role or family kind is wrong for downstream use.

failure_patterns.name: Wrong coordinate frame or orientation
failure_patterns.meaning: Mirrored views, wrong view direction, assumed camera, transforms defaulting to world axes.

failure_patterns.meaning: The layout is geometrically valid but cannot be built from stock material.

failure_patterns.name: API succeeded, model result wrong
failure_patterns.meaning: The call returned without error but Revit changed something else (auto-joins, ignored defaults, silent overrides).

failure_patterns.name: Correct model, unusable schedule or data
failure_patterns.meaning: Values exist but can't be scheduled, totalled or extracted.

failure_patterns.name: Correct element, wrong authority
failure_patterns.meaning: A value or decision was taken by the agent that belongs to the user, a standard or a discipline.

failure_patterns.name: Correct geometry, documentation fails
failure_patterns.meaning: Views, crops, dimensions or sheets don't show the model correctly.

failure_patterns.name: Source misread
failure_patterns.meaning: A dimension, view or note in the source document was missed or misinterpreted.

failure_patterns.name: Dependency not propagated
failure_patterns.meaning: A change in one element left dependents (profile walls, levels, hosted inserts, sheets) unchanged.

failure_patterns.name: Runtime blocked by a dialog
failure_patterns.meaning: A modal Revit dialog or warning blocked the automation; nothing visible in the API result.

failure_patterns.name: Fix incomplete
failure_patterns.meaning: The correction addressed one case of the problem; the same problem reappeared in a neighbouring case.

failure_patterns.name: Frame chosen from a name
failure_patterns.meaning: The agent picks the domain, discipline or meaning of a task from a familiar word (a name, an acronym, 'connector', 'panel', 'room', 'system') before inspecting the actual evidence, then executes valid operations in the wrong world. Rule: Identify -> Inspect -> Frame -> Act, not Recognize -> Assume -> Act.
failure_patterns.example: Given the link github.com/gschmidtke/ARPL, an AI described 'ARPL (Advanced Redpill Loader)', an unrelated NAS bootloader, without opening the repository, and even attributed that project to the wrong owner. Revit equivalent: 'create the equipment connector' read as electrical when the family is audio equipment.
failure_patterns.found_by: user noticed the answer did not match the source

failure_patterns.name: Exception leaves a transaction open
failure_patterns.meaning: A scripted error escapes while the script's own Transaction is still open. Inside an enclosing TransactionGroup this can crash Revit (fatal error) instead of failing the script. Defence: using-blocks for every Transaction, try/catch around the body, dry runs.
failure_patterns.found_by: Revit journal after a fatal error

failure_patterns.name: Shared assembly type edited through one instance
failure_patterns.meaning: Adding or removing members of an AssemblyInstance whose AssemblyType is used by other instances makes Revit ask (modal dialog, not a failure message) whether to update the type. The failures preprocessor cannot answer it, the API call blocks until a person does, and the change may be copied to every instance (members duplicated over the other instances). Defence: before editing members, count instances of the type; if more than one, create a new assembly from the new members instead and delete the old instance with its members.
failure_patterns.found_by: Bridge timeout; owner at the Revit dialog

failure_patterns.name: New assembly frame follows the project axes
failure_patterns.meaning: AssemblyInstance.Create gives the assembly a transform along the project X/Y axes, not along the element it describes. Assembly views (CreateDetailSection elevations, plan sections) and any dimensions computed in the assembly frame then look at the wrong side or collapse to one segment. Defence: after creating an assembly for a wall panel, call SetTransform so BasisX runs along the wall and BasisY points to the interior, before creating its views.
failure_patterns.found_by: West shop drawing came out with one stud dimension

failure_patterns.name: Modal warning raised inside an API call
failure_patterns.meaning: Some Revit API calls post a warning as a modal dialog during the call itself, before the script can change the condition (ElectricalSystem.Create checks the load against the default 20 A rating). The transaction's failures preprocessor does not see it; the bridge call blocks until a person answers. Defence: anticipate the condition (temporary small load, set limits first), and when a bridge call times out, look at the screen before anything else.

failure_patterns.name: Stale geometry references after regeneration
failure_patterns.meaning: Face references collected before other elements were placed on the same host can be invalid after a regeneration; using them for face-based placement throws a native SEHException instead of a managed error. Defence: fetch the host's face references immediately before each placement.
failure_patterns.found_by: SEHException that did not reproduce in an isolated test

failure_patterns.name: Unknown tool parameter silently ignored
failure_patterns.meaning: A misspelled or unsupported parameter (here mode instead of transaction) is dropped without an error, so the call runs with defaults: scripts that start their own Transaction fail inside the default wrapper. Defence: load the tool schema before the first call and check the reported transaction mode in the result.
failure_patterns.found_by: "Starting a new transaction is not permitted" from a script that had worked before

failure_patterns.name: Application reminder dialog blocks an automated run
failure_patterns.meaning: Revit's periodic "Changes Not Synchronized with Central" reminder is modal and stops a running command past the bridge timeout; a partial run can leave half-finished state (old views deleted, new ones not yet created). Defence: screenshot on every timeout, dismiss the reminder, read the model state before re-running.

failure_patterns.name: Read-only collection returned by the API
failure_patterns.meaning: ViewSheetSet.Views is a read-only ViewSet; Insert throws and, inside a TransactionGroup, rolls back everything before it. Defence: build a new ViewSet and assign it through PrintManager.ViewSheetSetting, and keep optional steps in their own try block.

failure_patterns.name: Long export outlives the call timeout
failure_patterns.meaning: A combined PDF export of 14+ sheets takes over 60 s; the bridge call times out while Revit keeps exporting. Defence: watch the status bar until it reads Ready, then check the file size and time before the next command.
failure_patterns.found_by: status bar progress in a screenshot

failure_patterns.name: Viewport outline inflated by elements outside the crop
failure_patterns.meaning: Section marks, camera markers and similar elements beyond the crop region set the viewport outline, so a rescaled view looks too big for its sheet; an automatic packer then moves it away. Defence: crop and annotation-crop first, find elements whose view bounding box extends past the crop, trim or hide them, and never empty a single-view sheet.
failure_patterns.found_by: sheet fit check plus an element search against the crop box

failure_patterns.name: Local cloud cache exhausts the disk during a batch run
failure_patterns.meaning: Every cloud model opened or synced is copied into the local collaboration cache (CollaborationCache under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\<version>). A batch over many models can fill the drive mid-run; Revit then fails saves or syncs in ways that look like model or network errors. Defence: check free space before a batch (several GB per dozen models), and let the user clear the cache with Revit closed; never delete it from a running session.
failure_patterns.found_by: user noticed under 100 MB free after an aborted batch relinking run

failure_patterns.name: Dependency inferred from a message string
failure_patterns.meaning: A help text, dialog message or log line names features that need a credential, licence or service, and the agent repeats it as fact. Such strings are often older than the code. Defence: confirm a dependency from the behaviour (does the command run without it?) or from the code path, and name the source when reporting it.
failure_patterns.found_by: the tool's author corrected the claim; the code path confirmed one command, not several
